subject: TPM staircase & pricing tied to MAP — SupplyChainAI evaluation to commit
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moore <alex@scai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff + target TPM staircase (draft attached)

Alex — thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, we'd like to put a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) on paper that ties the evaluation milestones to commit volumes and discount triggers so both teams have clear expectations for the pilot > production path.

Attached is a light draft (SupplyChainAI_MAP_draft_v1.xlsx) that proposes a staged commit (monthly TPM targets) with simple success criteria: accuracy on your benchmark, latency under 350ms p95 on the primary route, and a security checklist signoff. High level:
- Month 0–1 (evaluation): 5M tokens/month (POC sampling)
- Month 2–3 (pilot): 50M tokens/month
- Months 4–6 (ramp): linear ramp to 200M tokens/month by month 6

We haven't locked pricing in the sheet — want to understand what commitment flexibility you need. Primary asks from our side: target close date for a commercial commitment, and whether SupplyChainAI can accept a staged commit with a defined overage rate.

If this looks reasonable, I'd like to schedule a 30-min alignment with you and your procurement team next week to pin procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: SupplyChainAI_MAP_draft_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

From: Alex Moore <alex@scai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Crawford <ben@scai.com>, Priya Nair <pnair@supplychainai.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + target TPM staircase (draft attached)

Rishi — thanks for the clear starter. A few quick items from our side:

1) We like the staged approach but will need a softer ramp out of the gate. The engineering team prefers a 2-week canary at 25M TPM before moving to 50M to validate caching and latency at scale.
2) Pricing is the sticking point for us. We’re evaluating unit economics and need to know discount thresholds. Conceptually we’d expect: base rate for evaluation/pilot, and lower committed rates at 100M and 200M TPM thresholds.
3) Procurement timeline: Procurement can sign within 4–6 weeks once we have SOW + finalized MAP. We do run a short security/controls review — could you outline what evidence you can provide?

Can you share a pricing ladder and a short note on SOC2 / data retention? If you can carve a 30–60 day escape window tied to performance/regression risk during the ramp phase, that’ll help get internal buy-in.

—Alex
Head of Platform, SupplyChainAI
alex@scai.com

Date: 2026-05-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: internal: suggested pricing ladder for SupplyChainAI (redwood_pricing_tiers_v3.pdf attached)

Rishi — putting a pricing ladder on this thread so you can share a concrete commercial proposal. Key points in the attached PDF (summary below):

- Evaluation (0–1 month): $0.40 per 1K tokens (trial / POC rate)
- Pilot (months 2–3): committed 50M TPM at $0.30 per 1K tokens + overage $0.35 per 1K
- Ramp (months 4–6): staged commitments with guaranteed discounts: 100M TPM at $0.25 per 1K; 200M TPM at $0.20 per 1K
- Volume discounts trigger at sustained 90-day averages above the threshold
- Performance escape clause: 30-day performance remediation window; if key SLAs missed, customer can reduce commit by up to 25% during remediation period without penalty

Also proposed: an upfront minimum commitment credit to offset onboarding costs (one-time credit applied to first invoice).

I flagged a couple of items for legal re: termination language; we should avoid hard daily overage caps — prefer percent overage billing.

Attachment: redwood_pricing_tiers_v3.pdf (3 pages)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moore <alex@scai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed MAP + TPM staircase (updated) — please review

Alex — thanks for the quick notes. We incorporated your canary ask and added explicit milestone/decision gates so procurement can see the path to a signed commitment:

MAP highlights (high level):
- Week 0–2: Proof-of-concept (5M TPM), benchmark tests completed by your eng lead, success = baseline accuracy within +/-2% of your current model; billing at eval rate (see pricing).
- Week 3–6: Canary (25M TPM) — 2-week canary at 25M with monitoring runbook. If canary meets p95 latency <350ms and error budget, move to pilot.
- Month 2–3 (Pilot): committed 50M TPM/month (pilot rate) for 2 months; payment net 30.
- Month 4–6 (Ramp): staged increases to 100M then 200M TPM by month 6. Discounts materialize once sustained 90-day averages hit thresholds (100M, 200M).

Commercial terms (proposal):
- Pilot pricing: $0.30 per 1K tokens committed; overage $0.35 per 1K.
- Commit tier: 100M TPM -> $0.25 per 1K; 200M TPM -> $0.20 per 1K.
- Upfront onboarding credit: $15k applied to first invoice if PO is received within 30 days of SOW signing.
- Performance remediation: 30-day remediation window; if unresolved, customer may reduce commit by 25% for next billing period.

Requested next steps:
1) Procurement timeline and PO lead
2) Confirmation on SOC2 evidence needs (we can provide SOC2 Type II report + a short artifacts bundle).
3) If agreeable, we’ll put the MAP + SOW into DocuSign for signature.

Link to HubSpot opportunity (for procurement): https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/SC-2026

Thanks — I’ll be available Thursday for a call to walk through the MAP with Priya and Ben if that helps.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Rishi / Alex — quick procurement note from my side:

- SOC2 Type II report: please send redacted report and a short controls matrix. We have a one-week security window to review the artifacts.
- DocuSign: we prefer the MAP + SOW bundled into a single envelope. Can you populate contact details for invoicing (we need a billing contact and address)?
- SLA question: what availability SLA do you propose for the dedicated route? We need 99.9% monthly uptime for production.

One more ask: can you put the staged commit into the SOW as a table with explicit TPM by month and the corresponding unit price (makes it much easier for legal to consume).

If you can get us the redacted SOC2 and the SOW table by EOD Wednesday, procurement can target an internal approval the following week.

Thanks,
Priya Nair
Director, Procurement — SupplyChainAI
